To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Nb and NbN thin films are obtained under the same source conditions independent of the target state, and (ii) the effectiveness of the magnetron's magnetic trap influences the normal state electrical transport properties of NbN thin films.

(1) the stress of Nb and Nb N films can be kept at zero level over the lifetime of the target by keeping the sputtering pressure and the applied DC voltage constant, (2) the stress-free point shifts to lower DC voltage as the Nb target erodes, (3) the normal state resistivities of the NbN thin films can be reduced by increasing the magnetic field strength of the magnetron.

the deposition of high-quality Nb and NbN thin films can be achieved by reactive DC magnetron suttering from a new or an eroded target, provided the source conditions and the deposition rate are maintained constant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of reactive sputtering for superconducting electronic applications.
the influence of the source operating parameters on the properties of Nb and Nb N films.
the optimization of the deposition parameters for Nb and NbN thin films for superconducting electronic device production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in reactive sputtering processes, a constant deposition rate can be maintained by a proportional control of the reactive gas flow, while the deposition rate of a pure element is controlled by the DC power of the sputtering magnetron.
the quality of NbN films obtained in the reactive mode can be kept at a constant high level during the whole target lifetime if the sputter parameters are adapted to the target erosion.
the target lifetime is the only relevant parameter for the film quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of NbN films can be maintained over a long target lifetime by adjusting the deposition rate and the magnetic field configuration of the magnetron.
the quality of NbN films is not only determined by the sputtering conditions but also by the target condition.
Nb films with a low resistivity of 3 μΩ cm and NbN films with a critical temperature of 14.8 K and normal state resistivity as low as 100 μΩ cm can be produced at any state of a Nb target.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of the films is not influenced by the state of the target and that the deposition rate is the most critical parameter to be controlled during the reactive sputtering of NbN.
the quality of the films does not degrade as the Nb source erodes and can be kept at a high level for a long time.
the quality of the Nb and NbN sputtered films is not affected by the target state, but by the deposition parameters.
